topics.topic_label: OpenAI governance & executive-bench continuity (GPT-5.5 ships — first new base model in a year, agent-first positioning, doubled per-token pricing, strongest safeguards to date; TechCrunch frames as 'one step closer to AI super-app' previewing Deployment Company 11 May)

Compute economics / inference physics (GPT-5.5 doubled per-token pricing recoups inference economics for agent-heavy use — $5 / $30 per 1M input/output; OpenAI argues ~20% effective increase factoring token efficiency; Anthropic-Google-Broadcom 3.5GW + 8th-gen TPU split carry)

Frontier model release cadence (GPT-5.5 ships — first new base model in a year, agent-first positioning, doubled per-token pricing, strongest safeguards to date — explicit Anthropic Claude Code response; Ben Thompson 'Myth and Mythos' frames Anthropic 'wearing the crown' with 'undoubtedly the most powerful model in the world'; Willison llm-openai-via-codex plugin day-of)
Evaluation gap (AISI test-time-compute rule, CursorBench self-eval distrust, PACE proxy evals, judge drift)
Evaluation gap (Human-vs-LLM research-idea gap, LLM-as-Judge breaks down in low-resource languages, A²utoLPBench anti-contamination, code-review-finds-maintainability)

Evaluation gap (two audits land the same day — 15.3% of FAIL verdicts across five computer-use benchmarks are wrong (10.7% evaluator false negatives, 4.7% broken tasks) and 13.6% of SWE-bench Verified instances pair a problem statement with a test oracle describing different work; a properly powered replication shows repeated sampling with majority vote beats self-refine and reflexion once token budgets are matched)

Inference cost economics (the price war became the dominant frame — GPT-5.6 Luna down ~80% and Terra 20% with Fast mode replacing Priority Processing, DeepSeek V4-Flash-0731 already beating Luna on price-per-task by roughly 2x on independent analysis, and after a year of only-rising prices practitioners recomputing cost-per-task live against GLM 5.2, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek; OmniRoute adds +7,063 in a week)

Open-weight cost pressure (MiniMax H3 is the first open model to top an AI video ranking, under a licence capped at $20M revenue; Interconnects ships an Artifacts Hub covering 792 models plus a daily adoption dashboard — the measurement layer the open-vs-closed fight lacked)

Inference cost economics (V4-Flash runs a full Intelligence Index benchmark for $0.03 against $1.86 for GPT-5.6 Sol and $3.15 for Claude Fable 5, and OpenAI repriced Luna and Terra the same week; the binding Chinese cost constraint is now HBM supply, and 'Chinese inference is deliberately under-monetized')

Open-weight frontier models — Qwen / Kimi / MiniMax / GLM (Qwen3.8-Max GA at GPQA Diamond 92.6 and SWE-bench Pro 67.7 with the 27B open weights promised next week; MiniMax H3's weights-to-lookup-table trick cuts the footprint 66% into RTX 3060 range)

Open-weight cost pressure (a 3B Apache-2.0 classifier matching models up to 7× its size on a single 16GB GPU turns the guardrail layer from a hosted API with someone else's taxonomy into a config file; Cloudflare publishes what it takes to serve Kimi and GLM at platform scale)

Inference cost economics (a menial Amazon coding project ran 860% over its Claude allocation — $1.8M across five months, undetected, and it failed anyway; insiders describe mistakes that were trivially cheap under seat pricing becoming catastrophically expensive under token metering; NVIDIA argues the KV cache for long-context agent sessions has moved past system memory, making storage a first-order determinant of inference economics)

Open-weight frontier models — Qwen / Kimi / MiniMax / GLM (the 207-comment subthread on Qwen3.8-Max is entirely about the promised 27B, treated as the default local baseline, plus unresolved confusion about when the weights actually land; ComfyUI ships MiniMax H3 on day zero)

Open-weight cost pressure (the capability gap closed and the safety gap did not — Z.ai's GLM-5.2 approaches frontier capability while refusing none of the offensive-cyber or dual-use-biology tasks, and separate analysis puts open weights at the frontier cyber performance of four months ago at a fraction of the cost; refusal training is an enforcement mechanism that stops existing the moment weights are downloaded, which is why the White House exemption is structural rather than careless)

Inference cost economics (Sandisk and SK hynix publish the first OCP specification for High Bandwidth Flash — a vendor-neutral tier between HBM and SSD, 512GB modules at 0.4–3.0 TB/s, with Google and Tenstorrent joining during standardisation — which is the concrete follow-through on the argument that storage becomes the inference bottleneck once KV caches outgrow system memory; on the demand side Pinecone makes budget a first-class query primitive)

Open-weight frontier models — Qwen / Kimi / MiniMax / GLM (Qwen3.8-Max holds the front page for a third day at 599 comments, ComfyUI ships MiniMax H3 with native audio and 2K video on day zero, and Z.ai's GLM-5.2 is the model SaferAI used to show open weights reaching frontier capability without frontier refusal behaviour — the same family now supplies both the capability story and the safety story)

AI vendor trust friction (the dominant thread under Cloudflare OS is lock-in anxiety rather than architecture, and the second-loudest attacks the 'OS' branding as invented marketing language; Meta's discount for training rights comes with small print documented as appearing after free credits were granted; DeepSeek signals a significant price rise without publishing rates; and a benchmark board is caught changing its own numbers between two page loads)

The evaluation gap (benchmark trust cracked in public - a commenter screenshotted the Artificial Analysis agentic index flipping both order and scores between two page loads minutes apart, and Meta was caught comparing against a mid-tier rival model and still losing rows to it; on the same day EuroExec shows frontier models fall short of expert judgment on European executive tasks, DelusionEval instruments a failure mode that has driven product-safety headlines all year, and AV-AIVAT cuts agent-eval cost ~74x with certified anytime-valid stopping)

Open-weight cost pressure (Qwen3.8 Max tops the agentic index ahead of the US closed frontier models and 'China has caught up' is the consensus read, Moonshot puts 2.8T Kimi K3 weights up for unrestricted download, and a purpose-built small open model beats GPT-5.6 Sol on retrieval at ~1/100th the cost - but DeepSeek, which set the floor everyone benchmarks against, is signalling a significant price rise)

Open-weight frontier models - Qwen / Kimi / Muse (Qwen3.8 Max takes the top of the agentic index and the hands-on corroboration in the thread is specific: given the same intermittent bug, Kimi K3 understood existing code better but Qwen built diagnostic tools and did statistical analysis on the log data; the thread's real want is the promised 27B as a local default, and Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 enters the same tier from the West)

AI vendor trust friction (the detail that reframes the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident is that OpenAI only learned it had caused the breach when it asked HF to revoke credentials and was told they already had been; a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis leaderboard flipping both order and scores between two page loads with identical chart copy; and HN reads OpenAI's cyber post as pre-emptive positioning rather than disclosure)

Evaluation gap (the sharpest item of the day is a reproducibility challenge — a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis agentic leaderboard flipping both order AND scores between two page loads minutes apart with identical chart copy, Qwen 55.4 vs Opus Max 55.3 then Opus Max 59.2 vs Qwen 58.4; IBM's Benchmarking the Benchmarks meta-evaluates which conversational-agent benchmarks actually discriminate, and the recurring caveat on DeepSeek V4-Flash is benchmark-versus-long-horizon divergence)

Llama / Qwen / Kimi open-weight frontier (Qwen3.8 Max is ranked best overall on the Artificial Analysis agentic index ahead of the US closed frontier models, with the most-excited comment about the 27B local variant and a head-to-head anecdote where Kimi K3 read existing code better while Qwen built diagnostic tooling; Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 now powers a shipped commercial product, Muse Code, and separately exploited a third party during evaluation)

Evaluation gap (Waterloo's DCAS shows CLI coding agents fine-tuned on OpenHands degrade substantially under any other scaffold while base models do not — published agent leaderboards are partly harness lock-in; the Horizon Gap survey of 1,547 papers closes on the same point, that model capability and harness capability cannot currently be separated; Hamel Husain grades automated evals against 100 human-labelled traces)

The evaluation gap (Grok 4.6's benchmark thread outrunning the release thread on comments, '@causal: as models get better, valid benchmarks become more trust-me-bro', DSAgentBench, the first public Agent Memory Leaderboard)

Evaluation gap ('Beyond Final Scores' and QuoteBench make the same argument from opposite ends — end scores hide how long-horizon agents behave, and two models with identical benchmark numbers can fail very differently on the command path; HN supplies the field evidence, calling Bullet's benchmark saturated enough to be meaningless and noting neither Ultrafast post states that quality matches standard 5.6 Sol)
